parts: I don't think it's an issue with the data. Attached are two plots, both including the contours, tiles, and (critically) vlines and gridlines at each 45 degree integer multiple  starting at zero. One plot, "no180.png" emulates the previous plot in that the data have values for theta that are formed by seq(-180,178,by=2), while the second plot, "yes180.png" uses values for theta that are formed by seq(-180,180,by=2). In neither plot do the contour lines connect across the side of the plot opposite theta==0. In the "no180.png" plot, the vlines and gridlines are slightly off being perfectly parallel/perpendicular with the plot margins, as if they've been rotated clockwise a bit. In the "yes180.png" plot, the vlines and gridlines are fine except that there are two lines at the top, to each side of where one would expect the -180/180 line to appear.

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: disconnected contours with geom_contour()+coord_polar()
parts:
I think the problem is that in your data, theta goes from -180 to 178. So when you plot it, the ends don't quite join up:
ggplot(data = preds, mapping = aes(x = theta, y = phi, z = value)) +
    coord_polar() +
    geom_contour() +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(-180,180,by=45))


If you set the limits from -180 to 180, then it looks like they would join up, but there's a gap between 178 and 180 (or -180):

ggplot(data = preds, mapping = aes(x = theta, y = phi, z = value)) +
    coord_polar() +
    geom_contour() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-180,180), breaks=seq(-180,180,by=45))


If you add entries for theta=180 that are the same as theta=-180, then it looks like they join up:

p180 <- subset(preds, theta == -180)
p180$theta <- 180
p1 <- rbind(preds, p180)

ggplot(data = p1, mapping = aes(x = theta, y = phi, z = value)) +
    coord_polar() +
    geom_contour() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-180,180), breaks=seq(-180,180,by=45))



-Winston

messages.subject: Re: disconnected contours with geom_contour()+coord_polar()
parts:
I was able to hack a solution by computing the tiles by hand then using coord() instead of coord_polar(). The following function is very application specific (assumes names of data columns, range of plot, etc), but may be useful to others that encounter this issue in the future:

    polar_plot = function(data){
        dtheta = diff(sort(unique(data$theta)))[1]/2
        dphi = diff(sort(unique(data$phi)))[1]/2
        data$theta_lo = data$theta - dtheta
        data$theta_hi = data$theta + dtheta
        data$phi_lo = data$phi - dphi
        data$phi_hi = data$phi + dphi
        data$theta_lo[data$theta==min(data$theta)] = min(data$theta)
        data$theta_hi[data$theta==max(data$theta)] = max(data$theta)
        data$phi_lo[data$phi==min(data$phi)] = min(data$phi)
        data$phi_hi[data$phi==max(data$phi)] = max(data$phi)
        p = ggplot()+
        geom_rect(
            data = data

, mapping = aes(
                x = theta
                , y = phi

, xmin = theta_lo
                , xmax = theta_hi
                , ymin = phi_lo
                , ymax = phi_hi
                , fill = value
                , colour = value
            )
        )+
        coord(
            xlim=c(-180,180)
            , ylim = c(0,90)
            , subclass = 'polar'
            , theta = 'x'
            , r = 'y'
            , start = 0
            , direction = 1
        )
        return(p)
    }
    data = expand.grid(
        phi = c(0,1)
        , theta = c(-180,-90,0,90,180)
    )
    data$value = rnorm(nrow(data))
    polar_plot(data)
